Data Sources (free)` (lines 346-380). Not blocking: the actual `docs/Analyse.md` §6 footnote content this PR added is accurate and doesn't itself reference §9/§10 at all -- only the task JSON's own `decisions`-entry citation is mislabeled, so no reader of Analyse.md is misled, only a future task-worker/reviewer who tries to jump to '§9' to verify the precedent and lands in the wrong section. Fix: correct the section reference from §9 to §10 wherever it's repeated (this task's `decisions` entry, and consider a fresh corrective `decisions` entry on the now-done `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine-followups-followups` task per CLAUDE.md's append-only-correction convention, given its own `decisions` entry contains the same mislabeling).

decisions.decision: Corrected the mislabeled section citation ('§9's Screen 3 note (line 384)' -> '§10's Screen 3 note (line 384)') by appending a fresh corrective `decisions` entry to the now-done `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine-followups-followups` task's own JSON file, rather than amending that task's existing `decisions` entry text in place.
decisions.rationale: Confirmed against `docs/Analyse.md` directly: `## 10. This task's own checklist item asks to correct the reference 'wherever it's repeated' but explicitly frames the done task's own fix as 'consider a fresh corrective decisions entry ... per CLAUDE.md's append-only-correction convention' -- it does not call out the existing entry's own text as the thing to fix, so CLAUDE.md's 'Decision memory' default (append a brand-new entry, don't amend the existing one in place) applies rather than the narrower in-place-edit carve-out (which requires the checklist to explicitly name the existing entry's text as the target, as `backend-cftc-cot-data-followups` did for PR #274).
